walkthroughs.body_html:
Physiology, Coordination & Control — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physiology, Coordination & Control brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physiology, Coordination & Control.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Adrenaline binds to receptors on the membrane and activates:
options: DNA directly
Adenylyl cyclase to make cAMP
Ribosomes
Lysosomes

mcqs.q: Which gland is referred to as the master gland?
options: Pancreas
Pituitary
Thyroid
Adrenal

mcqs.q: What reads the mRNA codons during translation?
options: DNA directly reads the codons on mRNA and adds amino acids.
tRNA molecules carrying specific amino acids — their anticodons pair with mRNA codons at the ribosome.
Water moves both directions in the xylem depending on the time of day.
Ribosomes synthesise amino acids from scratch using the mRNA as a template.

mcqs.q: How does ADH affect the collecting duct in the kidney?
options: It increases the permeability of the collecting duct to water (by inserting aquaporins), so more water is reabsorbed and urine is more concentrated.
ADH actively pumps water out of urine into the blood.
Ribosomes synthesise amino acids from scratch using the mRNA as a template.
ADH directly opens holes in the collecting duct that let urine escape.

mcqs.q: Which direction does water move in the xylem, and what drives it?
options: Upwards from roots to leaves — driven mainly by transpiration pull (evaporation at leaves creating tension on the water column).
Ribosomes synthesise amino acids from scratch using the mRNA as a template.
Water moves both directions in the xylem depending on the time of day.
Water moves up the xylem because roots pump it actively using ATP.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Insulin”?
options: Peptide hormone from β cells of pancreas; lowers blood glucose by stimulating uptake and glycogenesis.
Peptide hormone from α cells of pancreas; raises blood glucose by promoting glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
Steroid? No: catecholamine secreted by adrenal medulla; activates fight-or-flight, raising heart rate and blood glucose.
Chemical messenger secreted into the bloodstream and acting on target cells with complementary receptors.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Glucagon”?
options: Peptide hormone from α cells of pancreas; raises blood glucose by promoting glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
Ductless gland secreting hormones directly into the blood, e.g. pituitary, thyroid, pancreas.
Chemical messenger secreted into the bloodstream and acting on target cells with complementary receptors.
Intracellular molecule (e.g. cAMP) that relays a signal from a hormone-receptor binding to enzymes inside the cell.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Second messenger”?
options: Intracellular molecule (e.g. cAMP) that relays a signal from a hormone-receptor binding to enzymes inside the cell.
Peptide hormone from β cells of pancreas; lowers blood glucose by stimulating uptake and glycogenesis.
Ductless gland secreting hormones directly into the blood, e.g. pituitary, thyroid, pancreas.
Chemical messenger secreted into the bloodstream and acting on target cells with complementary receptors.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hormone”?
options: Ductless gland secreting hormones directly into the blood, e.g. pituitary, thyroid, pancreas.
Steroid? No: catecholamine secreted by adrenal medulla; activates fight-or-flight, raising heart rate and blood glucose.
Chemical messenger secreted into the bloodstream and acting on target cells with complementary receptors.
Peptide hormone from α cells of pancreas; raises blood glucose by promoting glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Endocrine gland”?
options: Steroid? No: catecholamine secreted by adrenal medulla; activates fight-or-flight, raising heart rate and blood glucose.
Ductless gland secreting hormones directly into the blood, e.g. pituitary, thyroid, pancreas.
Chemical messenger secreted into the bloodstream and acting on target cells with complementary receptors.
Peptide hormone from β cells of pancreas; lowers blood glucose by stimulating uptake and glycogenesis.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Adrenaline”?
options: Steroid? No: catecholamine secreted by adrenal medulla; activates fight-or-flight, raising heart rate and blood glucose.
Peptide hormone from β cells of pancreas; lowers blood glucose by stimulating uptake and glycogenesis.
Peptide hormone from α cells of pancreas; raises blood glucose by promoting glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.
Ductless gland secreting hormones directly into the blood, e.g. pituitary, thyroid, pancreas.
